name: Keel Infrastructure Corp.

profile.description: Keel Infrastructure (formerly Bitfarms, rebranded April 2026) is developing large-scale powered land sites in North America into high-performance computing campuses for AI workloads. The company completed a transformative pivot from Bitcoin mining, decommissioning all U.S. mining facilities and exiting Latin American operations. Keel maintains a 2.2 GW development pipeline across Pennsylvania, Washington State, and Quebec, with $715.5M in cash and $1.04B in total debt. TTM revenue of $188M declining 50% YoY as Bitcoin mining winds down before AI data center revenue materializes. No signed tenant leases as of latest reporting. Headquartered in New York City. Market cap approximately $1.9B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Keel executed a transformative business model pivot from Bitcoin mining (Bitfarms) to AI data center infrastructure within 18 months — rebranding, exiting Latin American operations, decommissioning all U.S. mining facilities, and repositioning 2.2 GW of power capacity for hyperscale AI computing [1][2]. However, the transformation has yet to generate any AI data center revenue, Q2 2026 revenue declined 50% YoY to $30.4M with a $65M net loss, and no signed tenant leases have been announced [2]. Bold reinvention with unproven execution. AI Deployment (0/2): Keel does not deploy AI technology — the company builds physical data center infrastructure intended for AI workloads, which is capital construction, not AI product deployment [2]. No AI-powered products ship to customers and no AI-driven cost savings are reported. Market Share (1/2): Keel occupies a meaningful position in the emerging AI data center buildout with established grid interconnections in three regions, 2.2 GW pipeline, and Vertiv module acceptance at Moses Lake, but competes against vastly larger incumbents — Digital Realty ($45B), Equinix ($88B), QTS — with no operating AI data centers yet [1][2]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Specific development sites identified (Panther Creek PA, Moses Lake WA, Sherbrooke QC) with 96 MW Sherbrooke power capacity agreement and initial Vertiv modules being installed, but zero signed tenant leases — management describes 'active negotiations' which is pre-revenue [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Data center development is capital-intensive construction rather than technology research.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Keel states 'collaboration, accountability and community guide its culture' but does not articulate a distinctive mission or purpose beyond building AI data centers for commercial customers [1]. The pivot from Bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure was financially motivated — following market opportunity from Bitcoin margin compression to AI infrastructure demand — rather than driven by a deeper cause. Corporate messaging focuses on gigawatts, pipeline, and commercial tenants rather than an inspiring vision. Community Impact (0/2): References to 'ongoing dialogue around Sherbrooke' regarding community impact represent basic stakeholder management during facility development, not proactive community investment [1]. No charitable programs, foundation, or community investment initiatives identified. Employee Retention (0/2): No employee retention or tenure data available. The company underwent significant organizational restructuring during the Bitfarms-to-Keel transition including Latin American operations exit, likely involving substantial workforce changes. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful insider buying identified.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics — all core metrics score at or near floor, producing 0 independent of liquidity. D/E of 315.9% exceeds the 300% floor (score 0.0) after the $458M convertible note offering dramatically increased leverage [2][3]. ROE of -75.6% is deeply negative, well below the 0% floor (score 0.0, 2x weight). Profit margin of -230.6% is catastrophically negative (score 0.0). Revenue declined 50% YoY (score 0.0) as Bitcoin mining revenue evaporates before AI data center revenue materializes [2]. Forward P/E is negative (loss-making, excluded). PEG ratio unavailable (excluded). Estimated 5-year revenue CAGR of ~8% provides the sole positive contribution (score 0.87, 2x weight), but this is volatile crypto-driven revenue with no AI data center component yet. Daily dollar volume of ~$100.7M easily clears the $1M liquidity floor. The company's $715.5M cash position provides development runway but the $1.04B total debt and -$180.6M free cash flow represent heavy capital consumption [3].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Keel is building AI infrastructure — physical data centers, power interconnections, and land capacity purpose-built for AI and HPC workloads — making the underlying assets structurally immune to AI disruption [1][2]. The 2.2 GW development pipeline with established grid connections across three regions represents physical-world infrastructure that AI cannot replace, and AI growth directly increases demand for exactly what Keel offers: powered space for training and inference workloads. Regulatory permitting, utility agreements, and environmental approvals create multi-year barriers that software companies cannot circumvent. However, the company has zero operating AI data centers today — it is pre-revenue in its stated strategy — which introduces execution risk distinct from market structure risk. The assets are immune; the business is not yet proven. AI Opportunity (0/1): Keel generates zero quantifiable AI revenue as of Q2 2026. All current revenue is from legacy Bitcoin mining operations that are being wound down. Despite being purpose-built for AI workloads, no signed tenant leases or AI service contracts have been announced [2].

infinite_game.summary: Keel demonstrates one of the most dramatic business pivots in recent corporate history — transforming from a Bitcoin mining operation into an AI data center company — but this transformation was driven by financial opportunism (Bitcoin mining margins compressing, AI infrastructure booming) rather than a Just Cause. The company does not articulate a deeper purpose, and the organizational disruption of the transition suggests reactive adaptation to market conditions rather than infinite game thinking. By Sinek's framework, Keel is playing to win the AI infrastructure race, not playing to keep playing.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Keel articulates a business strategy — building AI data centers for hyperscalers — but not a Just Cause in Sinek's sense [1]. The pivot from Bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure was commercially motivated by the AI boom and Bitcoin mining margin compression, not driven by a vision of a better future. The company's messaging focuses on gigawatts, pipeline size, and commercial tenants rather than a purpose that inspires sacrifice or invites contribution beyond employment.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The Bitfarms-to-Keel transformation involved significant organizational disruption — exiting Latin American operations, decommissioning U.S. mining facilities, rebranding the entire company, and restructuring the workforce [1][2]. The hiring of Ganesh Aiyer (25-year Digital Realty veteran) as president suggests rebuilding rather than leadership continuity. While necessary for the pivot, this level of organizational change is antithetical to the psychological safety Sinek describes. No employee count, retention, or cultural data is publicly available.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Keel's competitive positioning focuses on its unique assets (power interconnections, site locations) without acknowledging the strengths of vastly larger competitors like Digital Realty, Equinix, or QTS [1]. The competitive narrative centers on Keel's advantages rather than learning from rivals. The hiring of a Digital Realty veteran as president implicitly recognizes competitors' strengths, but this is not reflected in management's public competitive framing.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The Bitfarms-to-Keel transformation is a genuine business model reinvention — abandoning Bitcoin mining entirely to pursue AI data center infrastructure, requiring country exits, decommissioning operations, rebranding, and accepting hundreds of millions in transition losses [1][2]. However, the pivot was driven by market conditions (Bitcoin mining margin compression, AI infrastructure demand explosion) rather than a Just Cause, making it strategic adaptation rather than cause-driven existential flexibility in Sinek's framework.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership led the decision to completely exit Bitcoin mining — the company's founding business — and bet the entire enterprise on AI data center infrastructure, accepting massive losses ($65M in Q2 2026 alone) and organizational disruption [2]. The $458M convertible note raise to fund AI development represents a significant leveraged bet. However, this is a single bet during obvious market tailwinds for AI, not a pattern of courage across multiple cycles, and the decision was driven by financial necessity as Bitcoin mining margins compressed.

investment_thesis: Keel at $3.05 with a $1.9B market cap is a speculative pure-play on AI infrastructure demand, offering a 2.2 GW development pipeline with established grid interconnections across Pennsylvania, Washington, and Quebec and $715.5M in cash to execute [1][2]. The Bitfarms-to-Keel transformation positions the company's physical power capacity for the most capital-constrained bottleneck in the AI supply chain — data center capacity with grid-connected power. The stock trades 59% below its 52-week high of $7.37, potentially offering a more attractive entry point for believers in the AI infrastructure thesis. The hiring of Ganesh Aiyer (25-year Digital Realty veteran) as president brings credible data center execution expertise, and the 96 MW Sherbrooke agreement and Moses Lake Vertiv module acceptance show physical progress [1][2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is overwhelming execution risk compounded by financial distress. Keel has zero signed tenant leases — the entire $1.9B market cap prices a data center business generating zero data center revenue [2]. Q2 2026 revenue of $30.4M declined 50% YoY with a $65M net loss as Bitcoin mining revenue evaporates. The financial profile is deeply distressed: D/E of 315.9%, ROE of -75.6%, profit margin of -230.6%, and free cash flow of -$180.6M represent a company burning cash at an alarming rate [3]. The $715.5M cash against $1.04B total debt provides runway, but continued development spending without tenant revenue could force additional dilutive capital raises. Environmental permitting delays (Panther Creek) and regulatory scrutiny of data center expansion create timeline risk. The company competes against Digital Realty ($45B), Equinix ($88B), and other massive incumbents with established tenant relationships. If AI capex cycles slow or hyperscalers build their own facilities, Keel's speculative pipeline becomes stranded assets. The Culper Research short report calling a similar company 'wildly overvalued' reflects broader market skepticism [3].
key_catalysts: First signed tenant lease at any of the three active negotiation sites would validate the business model transformation and could catalyze significant re-rating from speculative pre-revenue to contracted data center company [2]

Acceptance and energization of initial AI computing infrastructure at Moses Lake, Washington using Vertiv modules would demonstrate physical progress toward revenue-generating AI data center capacity [2]
Sherbrooke, Quebec 96 MW power capacity agreement and land purchase for consolidated data center campus leverages existing infrastructure at lower cost than greenfield development [2]
key_risks: Zero signed tenant leases despite months of negotiations — the entire $1.9B market cap is pre-revenue speculation that may not materialize as contracts, while the company burns $65M+/quarter with no committed revenue stream [2]

Financial distress with D/E of 315.9%, profit margin of -230.6%, ROE of -75.6%, and -$180.6M free cash flow — the $715.5M cash cushion could be consumed within 12-18 months of continued development spending, forcing additional dilutive capital raises or insolvency [2][3]

Competition against vastly larger incumbents (Digital Realty, Equinix, QTS) with established tenant relationships and proven execution — hyperscalers may prefer proven partners or build their own facilities rather than leasing from a pre-revenue startup with a Bitcoin mining legacy [1]
